author: Chase Foix
title: Dolly Parton's Imagination Library will continue through United Way of Siouxland - NewsBreak
text:
By Chase Foix Maren Ewertz ,
1 days ago
SIOUX CITY , Iowa ( KCAU ) — Dolly Parton was known around the world for her music, but her work helping children learn to read has also made a major impact, including right here in Siouxland.
Parton started the Imagination Library 30 years ago to help children in her hometown get access to books. That program grew quickly, and eventually expanded across the country.
Story continues below
The United Way of Siouxland brought the program to Sioux City 26 years ago. Since then, more than 11,000 local children under the age of five have taken part.
The at-home literacy program delivers one free book each month to preschool-aged children, with the goal of helping them prepare for kindergarten while encouraging families to read together.
Each book includes a special message from Dolly, along with tips for parents on how to read with their child.
"It really does kind of bring a tear to your eye when you have somebody with such a big impact pass away," said Heather Hennings, President of United Way of Siouxland. "And just knowing we've actually just this morning already received a notice from the Dollywood Foundation about the Imagination Library, and the fact that Dolly had planned for this and the program will continue."
To learn more about the Imagination Library's impact in Siouxland and how the United Way of Siouxland will continue to offer the program, click here .
